correctness.rationale: For all \(a>0\) and positive smooth uniform-marginal densities, monotone continuous \(Q\) gives unique Wardrop and social-optimal shares at thresholds \(a\) and \(2a\). Uniform-marginal event inclusions yield strict outer intervals. Two rotation copulas straddle any target; smoothing by positive wrapped circular noise and convex mixing achieves the exact target while preserving marginals. Monotonicity of Q gives strict between-equilibrium-and-one-half planner ordering. Boundary cases, tie probabilities, and strict nonattainment are checked explicitly; numerical checker is supporting only.

originality.rationale: Known fixed-marginal tail inequalities and fixed-copula congestion threshold characterizations are credited. The claim adds the sharp open set of endogenous Wardrop and social-planner flow shares for unknown dependence, constructive exact realization by strictly positive smooth copulas, and strict planner contraction for each common copula. Su–Mehr–Sastry and Bhattacharya–Makiranta state pointwise fixed-distribution results rather than quantified copula-identified sets; Makarov supplies the tail ingredient but not the endogenous attainable fixed points. Published-index searches found no dominating statement; residual priority risk documented.

value.rationale: Knowing each route valuation distribution without their joint dependence is a natural empirical data limitation in heterogeneous congestion models; sharp partial identification (not an arbitrary isolated numeric slice) is needed to assess route allocation. The theorem gives the complete attainable equilibrium and optimal-share sets for every congestion strength and proves a dependence-robust direction of the planner intervention. Smooth full-support realizability proves that the uncertainty is genuine even under regularity, while the strict balancing property is policy interpretable. It does not purport to yield all multi-route or nonlinear generalizations.
